entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9269"/><div sID="gen15852" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9269"/><hi type="bold">7. whom man despiseth--</hi>Hebrew, "the despised of soul," that is, by every soul, by all men (<reference osisRef="Isa.52.14">Is 52:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.52.15">15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.53.3">53:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.50.6-Isa.50.9">50:6-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.22.6">Psa 22:6</reference>). Lowth translates, "whose person is despised."<div eID="gen15852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15853" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">abhorreth--</hi>literally, "who is an abomination to the nation" (<reference osisRef="Luke.23.18-Luke.23.23">Lu 23:18-23</reference>). The Jews contemptuously call Him always Tolvi, "the crucified." I prefer, on account of Goi, the Hebrew term for nation being usually applied to the Gentiles, and that for people to the Jews (<reference osisRef="Hos.1.9">Ho 1:9</reference>; so the Greek terms respectively also Laos and Ethne, <reference osisRef="Rom.9.25">Ro 9:25</reference>), to take "nation" here collectively for the Gentile world, which also spurned Him (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.1-Ps.2.3">Psa 2:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.4.25-Acts.4.27">Ac 4:25-27</reference>).<div eID="gen15853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15854" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">servant of rulers--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Matt.17.27">Mt 17:27</reference>). He who would not exert His power against the rulers (<reference osisRef="Matt.26.52">Mt 26:52</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.26.53">53</reference>).<div eID="gen15854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15855" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall see--</hi>namely the fulfilment of God's promises (<reference osisRef="Isa.49.3">Is 49:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.49.6">6</reference>), "when He (shall be) a light to the Gentiles."<div eID="gen15855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15856" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">arise--</hi>to reverence Thee (<reference osisRef="Ps.72.10">Psa 72:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.72.11">11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.2.10">Php 2:10</reference>).<div eID="gen15856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15857" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">princes also--</hi>rather, for the parallelism, supply the ellipsis, thus, "Princes shall see and shall worship."<div eID="gen15857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15858" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">faithful--</hi>namely, to His promises.<div eID="gen15858" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15859" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">choose thee--</hi>as God's elect (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.1">Is 42:1</reference>). <div eID="gen15859" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. whom man despiseth-- Hebrew, "the despised of soul," that is, by every soul, by all men ( Is 52:14 , 15 ; 53:3 ; 50:6-9 ; Psa 22:6 ). Lowth translates, "whose person is despised." abhorreth-- literally, "who is an abomination to the nation" ( Lu 23:18-23 ). The Jews contemptuously call Him always Tolvi, "the crucified." I prefer, on account of Goi, the Hebrew term for nation being usually applied to the Gentiles, and that for people to the Jews ( Ho 1:9 ; so the Greek terms respectively also Laos and Ethne, Ro 9:25 ), to take "nation" here collectively for the Gentile world, which also spurned Him ( Psa 2:1-3 ; Ac 4:25-27 ). servant of rulers-- ( Mt 17:27 ). He who would not exert His power against the rulers ( Mt 26:52 , 53 ). shall see-- namely the fulfilment of God's promises ( Is 49:3 , 6 ), "when He (shall be) a light to the Gentiles." arise-- to reverence Thee ( Psa 72:10 , 11 ; Php 2:10 ). princes also-- rather, for the parallelism, supply the ellipsis, thus, "Princes shall see and shall worship." faithful-- namely, to His promises. choose thee-- as God's elect ( Is 42:1 ).

Messiah is represented as having asked for the grace of God in behalf of sinners; this verse contains God the Father's favorable answer.<div eID="gen15860" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15861" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">an acceptable time--</hi>"In a time of grace" [Hengstenberg]. A limited time (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.2">Is 61:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.6.2">2Co 6:2</reference>). The time judged by God to be the best fitted for effecting the purposes of His grace by Messiah.<div eID="gen15861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15862" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heard thee--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.2.8">Psa 2:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.5.7">He 5:7</reference>).<div eID="gen15862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15863" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">day of salvation--</hi>when "the fulness of time" (<reference osisRef="Gal.4.4">Ga 4:4</reference>) shall have come. The day of salvation is "to-day" (<reference osisRef="Heb.4.7">He 4:7</reference>).<div eID="gen15863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15864" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">helped--</hi>given Thee the help needed to enable Thee, as man, to accomplish man's salvation.<div eID="gen15864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15865" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">preserve--</hi>from the assaults and efforts of Satan, to divert Thee from Thy voluntary death to save man.<div eID="gen15865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15866" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">covenant of the people--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Isa.42.6">Is 42:6</reference>). "The people," in the singular, is always applied exclusively to Israel.<div eID="gen15866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15867" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">establish the earth--</hi>rather, "to restore the land," namely, Canaan to Israel. Spiritually, the restoration of the Church (the spiritual Israel) to the heavenly land forfeited by man's sin is also included.<div eID="gen15867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15868" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cause to inherit ... desolate heritages--</hi>image from the desolate state of Judea during the Babylonish captivity. Spiritually, the Gentile world, a moral waste, shall become a garden of the Lord. Literally, Judea lying desolate for ages shall be possessed again by Israel (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.61.7">Is 61:7</reference>, "in their land"). Jesus, the antitype of, and bearing the same name as Joshua (<reference osisRef="Heb.4.8">He 4:8</reference>), shall, like him, divide the land among its true heirs (<reference osisRef="Isa.54.3">Is 54:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.61.4">61:4</reference>). <div eID="gen15868" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 8. Messiah is represented as having asked for the grace of God in behalf of sinners; this verse contains God the Father's favorable answer. an acceptable time-- "In a time of grace" [Hengstenberg]. A limited time ( Is 61:2 ; 2Co 6:2 ). The time judged by God to be the best fitted for effecting the purposes of His grace by Messiah. heard thee-- ( Psa 2:8 ; He 5:7 ). day of salvation-- when "the fulness of time" ( Ga 4:4 ) shall have come. The day of salvation is "to-day" ( He 4:7 ). helped-- given Thee the help needed to enable Thee, as man, to accomplish man's salvation. preserve-- from the assaults and efforts of Satan, to divert Thee from Thy voluntary death to save man. covenant of the people-- (See on Is 42:6 ). "The people," in the singular, is always applied exclusively to Israel. establish the earth-- rather, "to restore the land," namely, Canaan to Israel. Spiritually, the restoration of the Church (the spiritual Israel) to the heavenly land forfeited by man's sin is also included. cause to inherit ... desolate heritages-- image from the desolate state of Judea during the Babylonish captivity. Spiritually, the Gentile world, a moral waste, shall become a garden of the Lord. Literally, Judea lying desolate for ages shall be possessed again by Israel (compare Is 61:7 , "in their land"). entries.reader_content_plain: 8. Messiah is represented as having asked for the grace of God in behalf of sinners; this verse contains God the Father's favorable answer. an acceptable time-- "In a time of grace" [Hengstenberg]. A limited time ( Is 61:2 ; 2Co 6:2 ). The time judged by God to be the best fitted for effecting the purposes of His grace by Messiah. heard thee-- ( Psa 2:8 ; He 5:7 ). day of salvation-- when "the fulness of time" ( Ga 4:4 ) shall have come. The day of salvation is "to-day" ( He 4:7 ). helped-- given Thee the help needed to enable Thee, as man, to accomplish man's salvation. preserve-- from the assaults and efforts of Satan, to divert Thee from Thy voluntary death to save man. covenant of the people-- (See on Is 42:6 ). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9286"/><div sID="gen15900" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9286"/><hi type="bold">24. the prey--</hi>Israel, long a prey to mighty Gentile nations, whose oppression of her shall reach its highest point under Antichrist (<reference osisRef="Dan.11.36">Da 11:36</reference>, 37, 41, 45).<div eID="gen15900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15901" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lawful captive--</hi>the Jews justly consigned for their sins (<reference osisRef="Isa.50.1">Is 50:1</reference>) as captives to the foe. Secondarily, Satan and Death are "the mighty" conquerors of man, upon whom his sin give them their "lawful" claim. Christ answers that claim for the sinners, and so the captive is set free (<reference osisRef="Job.19.25">Job 19:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.14.14">14:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.12.29">Mt 12:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.6.2">Ho 6:2</reference>, where <reference osisRef="Isa.49.4">Is 49:4</reference> shows the primary reference is to Israel's restoration, to which the resurrection corresponds; <reference osisRef="Isa.26.19">Is 26:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.4.8">Ep 4:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.2.14">He 2:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.2.15">15</reference>). Others not so well translate, "the captives taken from among the just Israelites." <div eID="gen15901" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 24. the prey-- Israel, long a prey to mighty Gentile nations, whose oppression of her shall reach its highest point under Antichrist ( Da 11:36 , 37, 41, 45). lawful captive-- the Jews justly consigned for their sins ( Is 50:1 ) as captives to the foe. Secondarily, Satan and Death are "the mighty" conquerors of man, upon whom his sin give them their "lawful" claim. Christ answers that claim for the sinners, and so the captive is set free ( Job 19:25 ; 14:14 ; Mt 12:29 ; Ho 6:2 , where Is 49:4 shows the primary reference is to Israel's restoration, to which the resurrection corresponds; Is 26:19 ; Ep 4:8 ; He 2:14 , 15 ). Others not so well translate, "the captives taken from among the just Israelites."

It was so mild that it required a large quantity to intoxicate; thus the idea here is that very much blood would be shed (<reference osisRef="Rev.14.10">Re 14:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.20">20</reference>).<div eID="gen15906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15907" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all flesh shall, &c.--</hi>the effect on the world of God's judgments (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.15">Is 66:15</reference>, 16, 18, 19; <reference osisRef="Rev.15.3">Re 15:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.15.4">4</reference>). <chapter eID="Isa.49"/>
entries.content_plain: 26. feed ... own flesh-- a phrase for internal strifes ( Is 9:20 ). own blood-- a just retribution for their having shed the blood of God's servants ( Re 16:6 ). sweet wine-- that is, must, or new wine, the pure juice which flows from the heap of grapes before they are pressed; the ancients could preserve it for a long time, so as to retain its flavor. It was so mild that it required a large quantity to intoxicate; thus the idea here is that very much blood would be shed ( Re 14:10 , 20 ). all flesh shall, &c.-- the effect on the world of God's judgments ( Is 66:15 , 16, 18, 19; Re 15:3 , 4 ).

It was so mild that it required a large quantity to intoxicate; thus the idea here is that very much blood would be shed ( Re 14:10 , 20 ). all flesh shall, &c.-- the effect on the world of God's judgments ( Is 66:15 , 16, 18, 19; Re 15:3 , 4 ).

navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 49 Is 49:1-26 . Similar to Chapter 42:1-7 ( Is 49:1-9 ). Messiah, as the ideal Israel ( Is 49:3 ), states the object of His mission, His want of success for a time, yet His certainty of ultimate success.
